{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3a4b6bc9b0975ceb2b5a22ae1ab3a918b88616ba88f20180477bcd7d65cc66ec","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:61","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving record and enforcement","heading":"C2 — Driving record and enforcement","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Driving record and enforcement

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A03
Do not stop at a crash unless involved or emergency help has not arrived, and do not obstruct responders. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A03
If involved in a crash, stop at or near the scene and move off the road if possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A03
Call police for an injury, death or vehicle requiring a tow; witnesses must seek help if injured drivers cannot call. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A03
Exchange driver names, addresses, phone numbers, registration numbers and insurance-company and policy details. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A03
Record names and addresses of other involved people and crash witnesses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A03
For damage to parked property, stop and seek the owner; if absent, leave a visible note with date, time, name and reachable phone number, and call police. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A03
If police do not investigate a crash involving injury, death or a tow, submit AA-600 within five days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A03
For a driver aged twenty-one or older, a BAC of 0.08 or higher constitutes DUI under the handbook's rule. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A03
DUI conviction may also occur below that adult BAC threshold when erratic driving supplies evidence of impairment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A04
Drivers younger than twenty-one meet the handbook's DUI threshold at BAC 0.02 or higher. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A04
Pennsylvania licensure carries implied consent to chemical alcohol or drug testing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A04
Refusing breath or blood testing after a DUI arrest can suspend driving independently of a DUI conviction. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A04
A first test refusal can bring a one-year suspension even when the DUI charge ends in a not-guilty result. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A04
DUI sanctions become more severe with higher BAC, greater crash harm and more convictions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A04
First or second DUI offenses require alcohol highway safety school at any impairment tier. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A04
Courts may order alcohol screening and treatment for DUI at any tier and may impose up to 150 community-service hours. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A04
A restricted-license interlock requirement generally means equipping every vehicle to be operated, or certifying no owned, registered or operated vehicles under PennDOT regulations. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A05
A first DUI offense at high or highest impairment may qualify for Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R19 | anchor: A06
People under twenty-one may not buy, consume, possess or transport alcohol, including in the vehicle they drive. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R20 | anchor: A06
Underage chemical testing after arrest and detention does not require parental consent, but police notify parents of the arrest. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R21 | anchor: A06
Courts may require alcohol evaluation and education, intervention or counseling for underage drinking. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R22 | anchor: A06
Knowingly and intentionally supplying alcohol to a minor can expose an adult, including a parent, to penalties. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R23 | anchor: A06
The Driver's License Compact coordinates member states and the District of Columbia to enforce licensing rules. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R24 | anchor: A06
Under the compact's one-license concept, an out-of-state license is surrendered when applying in another state. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R25 | anchor: A06
The compact's one-record concept keeps a complete record in the home state for resident and nonresident eligibility. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R26 | anchor: A06
Member jurisdictions report out-of-state driver convictions and license suspensions or revocations to the home licensing agency. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R27 | anchor: A06
Specified offenses in another member jurisdiction are treated as if committed in Pennsylvania for home-state sanctions. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R28 | anchor: A07
DUI preventing safe driving, failure to stop and aid after an injury or fatal crash, and a felony using a vehicle are among the compact's specified offenses. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-R29 | anchor: A07
Ignoring an out-of-state citation suspends Pennsylvania driving indefinitely until the required response is made to the cited location. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0089]
